title: Set 261

sentences.ko: 우리 고양이가 이제 내 노트북을 자기 침대로 정했나 봐. 그래서 일하려고 할 때마다 고양이를 옮겨야 하는데, 그러면 얼마나 삐지는지 그날 밤 내내 나한테 오지도 않아.
sentences.text: Our cat's decided my laptop is her bed now, so every time I need to work I have to move her, and she gets so offended that she won't come near me for the rest of the night.

alts.text: The cat thinks my laptop's her bed now, so I gotta move her every time I wanna work, and she gets so mad she won't come near me the whole rest of the night.
Our cat has decided that my laptop is now her bed, so whenever I need to work I must move her, and she becomes so offended that she will not come near me for the remainder of the evening.

sentences.note: **gets so offended** 는 사람한테도 고양이한테도 단단히 삐졌다고 할 때 써요. **for the rest of the night** 는 그날 밤 남은 시간 내내라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 캠핑 가기로 했는데, 토요일 내내 비가 퍼붓는대. 그래서 그냥 집에 있으면서 현관 앞에서 고기나 구워 먹으려고. 근데 오히려 그게 나을 수도 있어. 땅바닥에서 잘 사람도 없잖아.
sentences.text: We were supposed to go camping this weekend, but they're saying it's going to pour all Saturday, so we're just going to stay home and grill on the porch instead. Which might actually be better, because nobody has to sleep on the ground.

alts.text: Camping this weekend's off. It's supposed to pour all Saturday, so we're just gonna stay home and grill on the porch. Kinda better anyway, nobody's gotta sleep on the ground.

We had planned to go camping this weekend; however, heavy rain is forecast for all of Saturday, so we will remain at home and grill on the porch instead. That may in fact be preferable, as no one will have to sleep on the ground.

sentences.note: **pour** 는 비가 쏟아붓듯 내린다는 말이에요. **they're saying** 은 일기예보나 사람들 말을 전할 때 쓰는 ~래, ~라던데 정도의 표현이에요.

sentences.ko: 윗집 남자가 요즘 밤 열한 시쯤에 운동을 하는데, 몇 분마다 볼링공을 떨어뜨리는 소리가 나. 진상 이웃은 진짜 되기 싫은데, 조만간 한마디 안 하면 나 돌아버릴 것 같아.
sentences.text: The guy upstairs has started working out at like eleven at night, and it sounds like he's dropping a bowling ball every few minutes. I really don't want to be that neighbor, but if I don't say something soon, I'm going to lose my mind.

alts.text: Upstairs guy's working out at like eleven at night now, and it's like he's dropping a bowling ball every few minutes. I don't wanna be that neighbor, but if I don't say something soon I'm gonna lose it.

The gentleman who lives upstairs has begun exercising at around eleven o'clock at night, and it sounds as though he is dropping a bowling ball every few minutes. I would prefer not to be a difficult neighbor, but if I do not raise the matter soon, I fear I will lose my patience entirely.

sentences.note: **that neighbor** 는 다들 싫어하는 그런 유형의 이웃, 즉 진상 이웃이라는 뜻이에요. **lose my mind** 는 미쳐 버리겠다, 돌아버리겠다는 말이고 캐주얼에서는 줄여서 **lose it** 이라고도 해요.

sentences.ko: 이사 도와주고 싶어, 진짜로. 근데 그날 언니 애들 봐 주기로 이미 약속했어. 그래도 다음 주말에 짐 푸는 거 도움 필요하면 그건 무조건 도와줄게.
sentences.text: I'd love to help you move, I really would, but I already promised my sister I'd watch her kids that day. If you still need a hand unpacking next weekend, though, I'm totally in.

alts.text: Ugh, I'd totally help you move, but I told my sister I'd watch her kids that day. Need a hand unpacking next weekend? I'm in.

I would be glad to help you move, truly, but I have already promised my sister that I would look after her children that day. However, if you still require assistance unpacking next weekend, I would be very happy to help.

sentences.note: **I'd love to ~, I really would, but** 는 정말 하고 싶은데 못 한다고 부드럽게 거절할 때 써요. **I'm totally in** 은 무조건 할게, 콜이라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 점심 먹으면서 영상 하나만 보려고 앉았는데, 고개 들어 보니까 거의 네 시였어. 샌드위치도 다 못 먹었고, 뭘 봤는지 하나도 기억이 안 나.
sentences.text: I sat down to watch one video while I ate lunch, and when I looked up it was almost four. I didn't even finish my sandwich, and I couldn't tell you a single thing I watched.

alts.text: Put on one video over lunch, looked up and it was almost four. Didn't even finish my sandwich, and I can't remember a thing I watched.
I sat down to watch a single video while eating lunch, and when I next looked up it was nearly four o'clock. I did not even finish my sandwich, and I could not tell you one thing that I had watched.

sentences.note: **when I looked up** 은 화면에서 눈을 떼고 고개를 들어 보니라는 뜻이에요. **I couldn't tell you a single thing** 은 하나도 모르겠다, 하나도 기억 안 난다고 할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

reviewed: 2번 한국어: the ground 를 '바닥'으로 옮기면 방바닥처럼 읽혀서 '땅바닥에서 잘 사람도 없잖아'로 고침
3번 한국어: '운동을 시작했는데'는 그날 처음 시작했다는 뜻으로 읽혀서 has started 의 뜻에 맞게 '요즘 밤 열한 시쯤에 운동을 하는데'로 고침
4번 한국어: '나 완전 갈 수 있어'는 번역투라 '그건 무조건 도와줄게'로 고치고, note의 I'm totally in 설명도 '무조건 할게, 콜'로 다듬음
